text.p: These are the leading stories in the Moroccan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Cabinet discusses recent meeting of the Libyan-Moroccan commission and its decision to increase trade and investment exchanges.
- Former French Prime Minister Pierre Mauroy hails consolidation of Morocco's democratic institutions.
- The European Union and Morocco differ on judicial, technical and administrative aspects of the framework accord to upgrade the North African country's firms.
- Fuel station workers and suply companies set up two commissions in charge of solving differences.
- Prime Minister Abdellatif Filali and German Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt stress willingness to expand cooperation notably through joint ventures.
- State-owned airline Royal Air Maroc and Air France to improve quality and reduce costs.
- Association of Fruit and Vegetable Producers alarmed by drought in the southern region of Morocco.
- Casablanca urban commune expected to give the go-ahead to France's Lyonnaise des Eaux takeover of water and electricity distribution.
